solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resisting having status

blocks.note: with means having, as in a house with a garden
standing is one's status or rank in society

explanation.surface: Someone holds out against pressure because of their social position.
explanation.definitionFit: Withstanding something means holding out against it, so it works as a present participle synonym for opposing.

clue.text: Debris used to be there following evacuation

indicators.note: evacuating a word empties out its interior, leaving only its two outside letters

blocks.note: past tense of to be
the first and last letters of there

explanation.surface: Rubbish lay where something once stood after people fled the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the emptied word after the past tense; it sits in the answer's second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is discarded rubbish or leftover material, which is what debris amounts to as well.

clue.text: Itinerant reporter entertains wild party briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the party word is dropped
a host entertains guests by having them inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a teller is someone who reports or recounts things
a rave is a wild, energetic party

explanation.surface: A roving journalist hosts a shortened all-night dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened party goes in straight after the reporter's first letter, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant is used as a noun for a person who moves from place to place, which describes a traveller.

clue.text: Complacent broadcast feels as if it’s beginning to decline

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
broadcast also means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
first letter of decline

explanation.surface: A smug television programme seems to be starting to go downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone complacent is uncritically pleased with themselves and their achievements, which is exactly being self-satisfied.

clue.text: Although adults loathe babies, everyone is tiny to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points at the start of each word, so just the opening letters are taken

blocks.clueFragment: adults loathe babies, everyone is tiny
blocks.note: the first letters of the six words

explanation.surface: However much grown-ups dislike infants, we all started out small.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning even though, so it substitutes for although in a concessive clause.

clue.text: Daring dancing stunned lasses

indicators.note: dancers move about and change places, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some bold moves on the dance floor left the young women amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: Daring reads as an adjective but here it is the noun, boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring as a noun is adventurous courage, and dauntlessness is the quality of being fearless and undeterred.

clue.text: Where one might file bad reviews about writer?

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word is read backwards

blocks.clueFragment: Where one might file bad reviews
blocks.note: a bin is where unwanted papers such as poor reviews get thrown

explanation.surface: An author wonders where to put the scathing notices about their book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that writer is a stretch: the nib is the part of a pen that actually does the writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nib is the pointed metal tip of a pen that puts ink on paper, standing in for the pen itself.

clue.text: Cheers person getting paid to be a model

blocks.note: a pro, or professional, is paid for what they do
an artist's model sits for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone earning money for posing as an artist's model.
explanation.walkthrough: Prosit is a German and Latin toast, said when raising glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a drinking toast wishing good health, used exactly where an English speaker would raise a glass and say cheers.

clue.text: Obstruct everybody on street

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing placed on another comes after it, so the everybody word follows

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for street
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone out in the road is blocking the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay or hold up progress deliberately, so it works as a verb meaning to hinder.

clue.text: Fat babies regularly smudge clothes

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
clothes as a verb means covers or wraps, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to blur is to smear or make indistinct
first, third and fifth letters of babies

explanation.surface: Chubby infants keep getting their outfits dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly here means the odd-placed letters: first, third and fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubber is the thick layer of fat under the skin of whales and seals, and jokingly excess body fat.

clue.text: Second person caught sheep

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Another person was caught out over a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, so this is a specific example of the general animal.

clue.text: Lazy and not even dressed?

definitions.note: a jokey reading: lacking even a shift, a simple dress

blocks.note: first meaning: idle, lacking ambition
second meaning, read literally: without a shift, a loose simple dress or undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone so idle they did not bother getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is a simple straight dress or slip; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless describes a person who is idle and without drive or resourcefulness.

clue.text: Real idiot upset leader

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A genuine fool has unsettled the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader looks like a person in charge; in British papers it is the newspaper's main opinion article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a leader or leading article is the newspaper's opinion piece, also called an editorial.

clue.text: Rent somewhere in Croatia

blocks.note: first meaning: torn apart, past tense of rend
second meaning: the port city on the Dalmatian coast

explanation.surface: Paying for a holiday let on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid for housing, but it is the past participle of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port on the Dalmatian coast, and as a past participle it means torn, just like rent.

clue.text: Silence report of religious building in disrepair

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word sounding like the building

blocks.note: sh is the hushing sound for silence
an abbey is a monastery church

explanation.surface: Calls for quiet in a crumbling old monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby describes something worn out and run-down through long use or neglect, a state of being in disrepair.

clue.text: Dispossess some crime victims

indicators.note: some means a portion of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: Taking property away from people who have suffered crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant from their home, removing their possession of the property.

clue.text: His work is supposed to be done by someone else

definitions.text: His work is supposed to be done by someone else

blocks.clueFragment: His work is supposed to be done by someone else
blocks.note: surface reading: a boss who delegates, or an employee who shirks

blocks.clueFragment: His work is supposed to be done by someone else
blocks.note: setter's reading: his products are passed off as another artist's or signatory's work

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a lazy worker or a manager who delegates; in fact the work is a fake meant to pass as another's.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger makes copies of paintings, signatures or banknotes intended to be taken as genuine originals by another hand.

clue.text: Son is mixed up with Arab in scrapes

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so these letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, with joining it to the rest

explanation.surface: A boy has got caught up in trouble along with an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrapes looks like predicaments, but here it means grazes.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasions are grazes where skin has been rubbed away, which are scrapes as plural nouns.

clue.text: Singular type of number

blocks.note: first meaning: peculiar, strange
second meaning: a number not divisible by two

explanation.walkthrough: Singular suggests grammar, as in singular and plural, but here it means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd means peculiar or unusual, and an odd number is one that leaves remainder one when halved.

clue.text: Daughter understood the meaning of fear

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
read as in 'I read you', meaning understood

explanation.surface: A girl finally grasped what it is to be afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a noun for deep apprehension or terror about what may happen, so it serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Man on public transport performing for money

indicators.note: in an across clue a thing set on another comes after it, so the man word is placed second

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
a man in chess, the piece

explanation.surface: A fellow plays music on the bus, hoping passengers will pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A man is any chess piece, so the most important one serves here.
explanation.definitionFit: Busking is playing music or entertaining in public places for donations from passers-by.

clue.text: Main means of authentication is reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a seal stamped on a document proves it is genuine

explanation.surface: The principal way of verifying identity has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Main looks like an adjective meaning chief; in crosswords and old poetry the main is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: I left marriage finally, after former partner’s removal from home

indicators.note: finally points at the end of the word before it, so only its closing letter is used

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
taken as written
standard abbreviation for left
last letter of marriage

explanation.surface: Someone walked out at the end of a marriage after their ex was thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the I, L and E behind EX; the 's of partner's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is being banished from one's own country or homeland, a forced removal from home.

clue.text: Dish was for lad prepared by another

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
another lad, repeating the word just used

explanation.surface: A meal meant for one boy was cooked by a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' gives a second LAD, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Waldorf salad is a classic American dish of apple, celery and walnuts in mayonnaise, named after a New York hotel.
